text:
Mirobody

 Mirror your body in data. 

One standard, every source, one complete picture of you — building a lasting record to understand where your health is going. 
This open-source edition keeps that record on your own machine: lab reports, wearables and genetic files flow into it, and your AI agent can query it over MCP.

 English · 中文 · 日本語 

 
 
 

 ▶ Live demo · Try one command · Open in Codespaces · 100% local

 Try the engine with one command

No repository clone, Docker, model or API key. uv prepares Python and the package for you; the first run needs a network connection to download them. The resolver then works offline from the bundled vocabulary.

 血红蛋白 and ヘモグロビン both resolve to 718-7 . 血脂 stays unresolved: it names a category, not one test. The same engine standardizes names and units across the full app.

Your agent can then standardize any name, reading, unit or complaint you paste, on your machine and without a key. Reading a whole report also needs mirobody[parse] and a model key. Other MCP clients take the same command.

→ Use the engine from Python or MCP

 Try the full app in Codespaces

Run the web app in your browser with your own model API key. GitHub prepares the environment; you do not need to install Docker or Python on your computer.

 

1. Create the codespace and wait for the automatic setup to finish in its terminal. It starts the app, Postgres, the worker and the synthetic demo data.
2. Open the setup link printed in the terminal and enter your own model API key: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, DeepSeek, DashScope, or any OpenAI-compatible gateway. The key is saved only after a real request succeeds. The forwarded app port is private by default.
3. Sign in as you@mirobody.ai , code 111111 , on the Email code tab. Ask "How has my cholesterol changed?" The demo holds 2,019 readings across your record and mom@mirobody.ai 's, shared with you view-only.
4. Upload a synthetic sample from demo/upload/ on the Data page to see a new report join the record, or switch to mom's record and ask again.

The app and its records run in GitHub's cloud; the model service receives the documents and questions it processes. Use the included synthetic data to explore. Codespaces has usage limits and billing; model usage is billed by your model provider. Stop the codespace when you finish. For complete control on your own machine, use the local route below.

 Run everything 100% locally

 The app, records and models all run on your own machine. No model API key needed. Docker with Compose starts the stack and llama.cpp, with a small answering model and a document reader:

 

Allow 16 GB of memory, at least 8 GB of it for Docker. No GPU is required; on Windows, run the commands in a WSL 2 terminal. The first start needs a network connection to download container images and model weights. If the registry is not reachable from your network, deploy.sh says so and retries through a mirror; DOCKER MIRROR in .env names your own. After those downloads, document reading, standardization and answers run locally. CPU answers can take minutes; Mac, NVIDIA and Windows options explain how to use your GPU.

Open the app link the script prints. The local models are already selected; sign in with the same demo account above, ask a question or upload a sample. Which model to choose compares the local options.

 
 
 

 Prefer Docker with a cloud model? Run ./deploy.sh without a local model profile, then paste your own model key into the printed setup link. The app and records stay on your host; the model service processes your documents and questions.

Chat calculations take the original queried data directly. A cloud model's
code runs as JavaScript inside the app, with nothing to set up; a model on your
own hardware computes in Python in a local Docker container when the app can
reach a Docker daemon. Setup and data flow cover
both. Query views provide their built-in statistics without either.

install.title: Run without Docker
install.html:
No container, and nothing pulled from a registry. On Debian or Ubuntu, PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector comes from the distribution's own packages and the app runs straight from the checkout. It is the same install the Codespaces path performs:

git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody.git && cd mirobody
scripts/install_native.sh   # PostgreSQL, pgvector, the Python package, a .env
scripts/start_native.sh     # the worker and the app on port 18060

Open the link it prints and sign in as you@mirobody.ai, code 111111: the demo record is seeded already. A model key from the printed setup link adds document extraction and answers. install_native.sh installs system packages with sudo and writes one sudoers rule for the postgres account, and says so as it runs.

The local models belong to the Docker path, so this one answers through a model service. Everything else matches the row above it in what stays on your machine: the records live in the PostgreSQL you just installed, and a name to a code never leaves the machine.
